newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares rise among rosy future prospects.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares rise among rosy future prospects.

text.p: Egyptian share prices rose on Tuesday as investors began to recoup their position in the market among expectations of even more increases particularly after religious holidays in April, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index closed 3.01 points higher at 379.00 in average volume of 56.7 million pounds ($16.7 million).
"The market is promising. Prices are expected to go up by mid-May after the holidays," said Ahmed el-Helw, managing director of Intercapital.
"Prices will move up after the moslem feast Eid al-Adha," said Yasser Rashed of Triple A Securities.
Moslems will celebrate the Eid al-Adha feast, expected to start on April 17, and then the market will also close when Coptic Christians mark Easter later this month.

Cement firms dominated trading again after a lull and brokers predicted they would remain investor favourites for a long time. "This year will be the cement year, with a lot of large government projects to be implemented," Rashed said.
"They are in strong demand by foreigners and their prices are expected to increase sharply," he added.
Helwan Portland Cement was the most active cement stock, with shares worth 3.7 million pounds traded. The share ended 1.00 pound up at 79.
Amriyah Cement closed unchanged after 2.7 million pounds of shares exchanged hands. "Amriyah is in strong demand," Rashed said.
Egyptian Tora Portland Cement ended down 1.03 pounds at 96.95.

Misr International Bank/MIBANK, another active share, shed 34.3 pounds to close at 651.6. The bank has been loosing ground since Thursday, the last day for shareholders to be eligible for a one-for-two bonus share.
The price stood at about 750 pounds last week.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 573.5 points from 564.39 points on Sunday. The index for rarely traded "closed" firms also rose to 265.6 from 264.71.
Out of the 83 shares traded on Tuesday, 32 gained, 26 lost and 25 ended unchanged.
